_meta.active: COBICISTAT; ELVITEGRAVIR; EMTRICITABINE; TENOFOVIR ALAFENAMIDE FUMARATE
_meta.indication: Indicated as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older who have no antiretroviral treatment history or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically-suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable regimen for at least 6 months

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 104 and Study 111 (pooled), in treatment-naive adults
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trials; subjects randomized 1:1 to GENVOYA or STRIBILD once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Antiretroviral treatment-naive HIV-1 infected adults; mean age 36 years, 85% male
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 (snapshot analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48: 92% GENVOYA vs 90% STRIBILD; treatment difference 2.0% (95% CI: -0.7% to 4.7%), establishing non-inferiority

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 109, in virologically-suppressed adults switched to GENVOYA
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to switch to GENVOYA or stay on baseline regimen
pivotal_trials.population: Virologically-suppressed (HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL) HIV-1 infected adults suppressed for at least 6 months on baseline regimen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Maintenance of virologic suppression (HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL) at Week 48
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 48, 96% of patients who switched to GENVOYA had HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL compared to 93% of patients who remained on baseline regimen

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (incidence >= 10%) is nausea (10% GENVOYA vs 13% STRIBILD); other common reactions include diarrhea (7% vs 9%), headache (6% vs 5%) and fatigue (5% vs 4%). Serious warnings include new onset or worsening renal impairment and bone loss/mineralization defects.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of elvitegravir (HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor), cobicistat (CYP3A inhibitor/pharmacokinetic enhancer), and emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide (both HIV-1 nucleoside/nucleotide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitors)

boxed_warning.content: Lactic acidosis/severe hepatomegaly with steatosis (including fatal cases) reported with nucleoside analogs, and post-treatment severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B in patients coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV who discontinue emtricitabine and/or tenofovir products; GENVOYA is not approved for treatment of chronic HBV

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not presented before the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee as no significant clinical or safety issues warranted discussion

summary.text: Standard NDA submitted November 5, 2014 with a PDUFA goal date of November 5, 2015, approved November 5, 2015 as a full (traditional) approval for a fixed-dose combination containing new molecular entity tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) with three previously approved drugs; no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote:
Date of Submission	November 5, 2014
PDUFA Goal Date	November 5, 2015

Genvoya contains three previously approved drugs and one new molecular entity: elvitegravir (EVG), an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor; coabistat (COBI), a CYP 3A inhibitor; emtricitabine (FTC), a nucleoside analog reverse transcriptase inhibitor, in addition to the new tenofovir (TFV) prodrug, tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF).

The application was not presented before the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee because a preliminary review of the NDA, including labeling, did not reveal any significant clinical or safety issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.
